pattern.top_pattern: Behavioral health admissions and acuity are rising across NC, GA, VA, NY, IA, and WV
pattern.what_is_impacting: Medicaid IP BH and ACUTE PSYCH
pattern.pattern_details: Behavioral health is a recurring cost theme across multiple states, with both inpatient behavioral health and acute psych facility growth. North Carolina and Virginia are led by depressive, stress, and adjustment-related admissions, while Georgia is concentrated at RIDGEVIEW INSTITUTE MONROE across both acute psych products and inpatient behavioral health. Smaller acute psych increases in New York, Iowa, and West Virginia show the same pattern of rising admissions with added unit-cost pressure.
pattern.why_it_matters: This is a scalable UM and network management opportunity because the same behavioral health pattern is repeating across products, facilities, and states.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Run a focused behavioral health action plan covering admission criteria, length-of-stay management, and provider concentration for IP BH and ACUTE PSYCH, starting with NC, VA, and RIDGEVIEW INSTITUTE MONROE in GA.
evidence_summary: NC IP BH added +$1.5M, led by PTSD at +$684K and adjustment disorder with mixed disturbance of emotions at +$486K, with more admissions and higher paid per admit.
VA IP BH added +$1.1M, led by major depressive disorder at +$581K and depression unspecified at +$503K.
GA behavioral health totaled +$1.9M across RIDGEVIEW INSTITUTE MONROE, including +$620K in TANF Standard acute psych and +$414K in TANF Foster Care acute psych.
NY, IA, and WV acute psych added another +$959K combined under ABD Non Dual or TANF Standard, with admissions and paid per admit rising.
